description: We’re a two-person team building CrewPulse, a React Native prototype to help astronauts log daily health checks and track changes in heart rate and balance during long missions. I’m Md Hasan Zaker, a software engineering master’s student at Memorial University with full-stack development experience. We welcome teammates with skills in mobile development, UI/UX design, data visualization, or health sciences to help us build and test the app.
summary: CrewPulse is an offline Android prototype that helps astronauts spot gradual changes in their health during long missions. A guided daily check-in combines phone-based heart rate, reaction time, balance, and breathing checks with manually entered health readings. The app compares results with reference ranges and, when enough recent readings are available, each astronaut’s personal baseline. A color-coded body map shows what changed, explains why it was flagged, and displays 30-day trends. NASA Human Research Program resources guided our choice of indicators. The demo uses fictional crew records and simulates reporting a flagged result to a flight surgeon under different communication delays.
details:
An astronaut starts a guided check-in. CrewPulse uses the camera and flash to estimate pulse, the touchscreen for a reaction-time test, and the accelerometer for balance and breathing checks. Crew members enter blood pressure, blood glucose, temperature, sleep, mood, and stress.

The app applies fixed rules to compare each result with a reference range and, when enough measurements are available, a personal baseline from the past seven days. It can look back up to 14 days when readings are sparse. The interactive body map shows flagged readings, explains the reason and relevant NASA spaceflight risk, and displays 30-day trends. For example, short sleep paired with slower reactions can flag a possible fatigue pattern.

The demo uses fictional crew records and simulates sending a flagged result to a flight surgeon under ISS, Moon, and Mars communication delays. We built the Android prototype with Expo, React Native, and TypeScript. VisionCamera and Expo Sensors collect phone readings, SQLite stores them on the device, and React Native SVG renders the body map and trends. We designed the app to work offline and explain each alert so crews can review changes and decide when to seek help from the ground.
dataRefs: NASA HRP Risks of Human Spaceflight
